extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying peer review, scientometrics, journal editors, and meta-researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing linguistic characteristics of large corpus of peer review reports (472,449 reports) to study how features such as tone, sentiment, morality, length, and reviewer/review-type variables relate to reviewer recommendations and other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count (report length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word count (mean and 95% confidence interval; LIWC analysis) of peer review reports in four broad areas of research for double-blind and single-blind review, and for female and male reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports recommending accept were consistently the shortest, and reports recommending major revisions were consistently the longest. Supplementary file 1 contains summary data and mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical tone (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical tone scores returned by LIWC (mean percentages and 95% confidence interval) for peer review reports across research areas, reviewer gender, and review type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed in Figure 2 (panel A). See Supplementary files 2–4 for summary data, mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals, and examples of reports with high and low analytical tone scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clout (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clout scores returned by LIWC (mean percentages and 95% confidence interval) for peer review reports across research areas, reviewer gender, and review type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports recommending accept consistently had the most clout, and reports recommending reject consistently had the least clout. See Supplementary files 2–4 for summary data, regression coefficients, residuals, and example reports with high/low clout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity scores returned by LIWC (mean percentages and 95% confidence interval) for peer review reports across research areas, reviewer gender, and review type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed in Figure 2 (panel C). Supplementary files 2–4 include summary data, mixed model coefficients, residuals, and examples of reports with high and low authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment scores as returned by LIWC (mean percentage and 95% CI) for peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as one of three sentiment measures (LIWC, SentimentR, Stanford CoreNLP) in Figure 3. See Supplementary files 5–7 for summary data, mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals, and examples of reports with high and low sentiment according to LIWC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment (SentimentR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment scores produced by the SentimentR package (mean score and 95% CI) for peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented alongside LIWC and Stanford CoreNLP sentiment measures in Figure 3. See Supplementary files 5–7 for full summary data, regression coefficients and residuals, and example reports illustrating high/low scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment (Stanford CoreNLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment scores produced by Stanford CoreNLP (mean score and 95% CI) for peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as the third sentiment measure in Figure 3. Supplementary files 5–7 contain supporting summary data, statistical model outputs, and examples of reports with extreme sentiment scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: General morality (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores returned by LIWC for general morality in peer review reports (mean percentage on a log scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports recommending accept consistently had the highest general morality scores. Supplementary file 8 lists the ten most frequent words found in peer review reports for general morality and the five moral foundation variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation: care/harm (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC-derived score for the care/harm moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed in Figure 4—figure supplement 1. Supplementary file 8 provides word lists and further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation: fairness/cheating (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC-derived score for the fairness/cheating moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed in Figure 4—figure supplement 2. See Supplementary file 8 for the most frequent words and additional data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation: loyalty/betrayal (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC-derived score for the loyalty/betrayal moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed in Figure 4—figure supplement 3. Supplementary file 8 lists frequent words and related analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation: authority/subversion (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC-derived score for the authority/subversion moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed in Figure 4—figure supplement 4. See Supplementary file 8 for word lists and summary statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation: sanctity/degradation (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC-derived score for the sanctity/degradation moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed in Figure 4—figure supplement 5. Supplementary file 8 contains the ten most frequent words and further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recommendation category
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorical reviewer recommendation (e.g., accept, major revisions, reject) used as a variable in analyses of linguistic characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer recommendation had the biggest impact on the linguistic characteristics of reports. Specific observed patterns: accept recommendations associated with shortest reports, highest clout, and highest general morality scores; major revisions associated with the longest reports; reject associated with lowest clout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area of research / discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad area of research (HMS: health and medical sciences; LS: life sciences; PS: physical sciences; SS&E: social sciences and economics) used as a factor in analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area of research had little or no impact on the linguistic characteristics of reports, which the authors interpret as a sign of the robustness of peer review. Figures compare scores across the four areas for single- and double-blind review and by reviewer gender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of peer review (single-blind vs double-blind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review type (single-blind versus double-blind) included as a factor in the linguistic analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures present results separately for double-blind and single-blind review. The type of peer review had little or no impact on the linguistic characteristics according to the study's findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer gender (female vs male) treated as a factor when analyzing linguistic characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses compare scores for female and male reviewers; the study found reviewer gender had little or no impact on linguistic characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement tools and multi-method sentiment approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of multiple text-analysis tools to quantify linguistic features: LIWC for analytical tone, clout, authenticity, morality, and LIWC sentiment; SentimentR and Stanford CoreNLP for additional sentiment measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper applies LIWC metrics alongside SentimentR and Stanford CoreNLP to triangulate sentiment and other linguistic features. Supplementary files provide model outputs, coefficients, residuals, and example reports illustrating high and low scores for each tool/metric.
